qt: to the Commission Gianantonio Da Re (ID) Subject:

The stated priorities of the Belgian Presidency of the Council of the European Union for culture and sports are to enhance and develop the European Education Area with the aim of promoting lifelong learning and helping to effect the digital transition in the cultural sector. In particular, the Belgian Presidency claims to want to adopt a new ‘European sport model’. Can the Commission therefore say: 1.
What view it takes of that project, and
What steps it intends to take to make it a reality?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.3.2024) In the area of sport, the Council, during the Belgian Presidency, will work on the EU Work Plan for Sport 2024-2027 and discuss the role of non-organised sport and free physical activity and their relation to a European Sport Model. The Commission is committed to keep promoting the European Sport Model characterised by key features1, such as the openness of competitions based purely on sporting merit and results; the pyramidal organisation of sport; its autonomy and solidarity between grassroots and elite sports.
1 Further to the Council Resolution on the key features of a European Sport Model,
